exposure: Timing of pregnancy (early third trimester, late third trimester, post-delivery)
outcome: Various clinical biochemical parameters (e.g., blood cell counts, hormone levels, liver and kidney function markers: neutrophil, triiodothyronine (T3), thyroxine (T4), testosterone, estradiol, progesterone, RBC, hemoglobin (Hb), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), creatinine (Cr), platelet, insulin, aspartate aminotransferase (AST), thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), free T4, FSH, luteinizing hormone (LH))
cohort: 993 pregnant Taiwanese women participating in the Taiwan Maternal and Infant Cohort Study, recruited from nine hospitals across Taiwan between 2012 and 2015.
finding: The study established gestation-specific reference intervals for various biochemical parameters in pregnant Taiwanese women and found significant changes in these parameters when comparing early third trimester, late third trimester, and post-delivery states.
followup_time: After delivery (exact time not specified) for a subset of women
gest_age: Weeks 28-40 of gestation, with specific comparisons at weeks 28-31 (early third trimester) and weeks 37-40 (late third trimester)
